title: Human Bias in the Face of AI: Examining Human Judgment Against Text Labeled as AI Generated

live_model.evidence: "we sent each entry to three major LLMs accessed by API keys between August 10 and August 17, 2024 -- Gpt-4o-2024-05-13 (ChatGPT), Claude-2 (Claude), and Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (Llama)"; 200 entries/dataset x 3 datasets.

prompt.location: Sec 2.1: task instructions paraphrased ("asked to rephrase them for readability", "instructed to write summaries", "instructed to write persuasive articles"); "instructed to generate content with lengths similar to human-written content"
prompt.note: Task instructions are described but not quoted verbatim.

claim.metric: none automated; the paper's dependent variable is human raters' bias/misattribution rate
claim.location: Sec 2.2-3 (Mechanical Turk study design); Table 1 gives only word-count descriptive stats, not a capability score

data.source: Wikipedia-intro, CNN/DailyMail, and a persuasive-essay dataset, all via Hugging Face

notes: gpt-4o-2024-05-13's own text-generation step is clean and reproducible (200 items x 3 scenarios via API), but the paper's actual claim is about human (MTurk) bias in judging AI- vs human-written text, not a score attributable to the model itself; no automated/model-based metric is reported as an alternative.
